lines: Two-channel bridge between the patch and an audio device, sending two signals out to it and bringing two back
Scales the signal sent to the audio device, from silence at one end of its travel to +12dB at the other, with unity gain in the middle
Sent to the first output channel of the audio device, 10V being full scale; with RIGHT unpatched this signal is sent to both channels
Sent to the second output channel of the audio device, 10V being full scale
Carries the first input channel of the audio device, full scale arriving as 10V
Carries the second input channel of the audio device, full scale arriving as 10V
Note — the driver, device, sample rate and block size are chosen on the display in the upper part of the panel; a larger block size adds latency and makes dropouts less likely
Menu — Master audio module makes this module drive the engine's timing; DC blocker strips any constant offset from the signal sent to the device, and is on by default here
Eight-channel bridge between the patch and an audio device, sending eight signals out to it and bringing eight back
Sent to the audio device's output channel of that number, 10V being full scale
Carries the audio device's input channel of that number, full scale arriving as 10V
Note — the driver, device, sample rate and block size are chosen on the display in the upper part of the panel; a larger block size adds latency and makes dropouts less likely
Note — the lamp beside a pair of jacks is green while the chosen device has those two channels, and red for a quarter of a second after the signal passes full scale
Menu — Master audio module makes this module drive the engine's timing; DC blocker strips any constant offset from the signals sent to the device
Sixteen-channel bridge between the patch and an audio device, sending sixteen signals out to it and bringing sixteen back
Sent to the audio device's output channel of that number, 10V being full scale
Carries the audio device's input channel of that number, full scale arriving as 10V
Note — the driver, device, sample rate and block size are chosen on the display in the upper part of the panel; a larger block size adds latency and makes dropouts less likely
Note — the lamp beside a pair of jacks is green while the chosen device has those two channels, and red for a quarter of a second after the signal passes full scale
Menu — Master audio module makes this module drive the engine's timing; DC blocker strips any constant offset from the signals sent to the device
Turns the notes, wheels and clock of a MIDI device into control voltages
The pitch of the note being played, a volt per octave with middle C at 0V; the pitch bend wheel is added to it
10V while a note is held and 0V once it is released
The velocity of the note played, 0V to 10V across MIDI velocity 0 to 127
Channel pressure from the MIDI device, 0V to 10V across MIDI values 0 to 127
The position of the pitch bend wheel, -5V to +5V, resting at 0V
The position of the mod wheel, 0V to 10V across MIDI values 0 to 127
A 1ms 10V pulse on every MIDI clock tick, which is 24 ticks to the quarter note
A 1ms 10V pulse on one MIDI clock tick in every 24, giving a pulse per quarter note; the menu offers divisions from a whole note to every tick
A 1ms 10V pulse each time a note is pressed, so an envelope can be restarted during a held phrase
A 1ms 10V pulse when the MIDI device sends a start message
A 1ms 10V pulse when the MIDI device sends a stop message
A 1ms 10V pulse when the MIDI device sends a continue message
Note — the MIDI driver, device and channel are chosen on the display in the upper part of the panel
Menu — Polyphony channels sets how many notes sound at once and how many channels the note outputs carry; Polyphony allocation and Monophonic priority govern which note goes where
Menu — Pitch bend range sets how far the wheel bends V/OCT, from off to four octaves; Smooth pitch/mod wheel slews the wheel outputs; Reset MIDI (Panic) drops every held note
Turns sixteen MIDI CC controllers into control voltages, one per cell of the grid
The value of the CC number printed in the cell above, 0V to 10V across MIDI values 0 to 127; the gamepad driver sends values that reach down to -10V
Note — click a cell and move a control on the MIDI device to assign that CC number to it, or type the number in directly
Menu — Smooth CC slews each output rather than stepping it; 14-bit CC 0-31 / 32-63 pairs each low CC with the one 32 above it for finer resolution
Menu — MPE mode gives each of the sixteen MIDI channels its own polyphony channel on every output
Turns sixteen MIDI notes into separate gates, one per cell of the grid, for driving drum voices from a pad controller
10V while the note printed in the cell above is held; the menu can make it a 1ms trigger at each press instead, or scale the voltage by velocity or aftertouch
Note — click a cell and play a note on the MIDI device to assign that note to it
Menu — Output type switches between gates and 1ms triggers; Output amplitude sets whether a gate is a flat 10V or scaled by velocity or aftertouch; Reset MIDI (Panic) drops every held note
Drives knobs and sliders of other modules in the patch from the CC controllers of a MIDI device, with no cables and no jacks
Note — click an empty row, then click the knob to be driven, then move a control on the MIDI device; the row then names the CC number and the parameter it drives
Menu — Smooth CC slews the mapped parameter towards each new CC value rather than stepping it
Turns voltages in the patch into MIDI sent out to a device, so a hardware synthesiser can be played from Rack
Sets the pitch of the note sent out, a volt per octave with middle C at 0V; the number of channels patched here sets how many notes are sent at once
Rising past 1V sends a note on, and falling back below sends a note off
Sets the velocity of the note sent, 0V to 10V across MIDI velocity 0 to 127; with nothing patched the velocity sent is 100
Sets the key pressure sent for the held note, 0V to 10V across MIDI values 0 to 127
Sets the pitch wheel sent, -5V to +5V across its whole range, centred at 0V
Sets the mod wheel sent, 0V to 10V across MIDI values 0 to 127
Each rise past 1V sends one MIDI clock tick, so 24 pulses to the quarter note clock the device at the patch tempo
Sets the MIDI volume controller sent, 0V to 10V across MIDI values 0 to 127; with nothing patched it sends the maximum
Sets the MIDI pan controller sent, -5V to +5V, centred at 0V
Rising past 1V sends a MIDI start message
Rising past 1V sends a MIDI stop message
Rising past 1V sends a MIDI continue message
Note — the MIDI driver, device and channel are chosen on the display in the upper part of the panel
Menu — Reset MIDI (Panic) sends a note off for every note this module has sent on, which clears a stuck note on the device
Turns sixteen voltages from the patch into MIDI CC messages sent out to a device, one per cell of the grid
0V to 10V sets the value 0 to 127 of the CC number printed in the cell above, sent out whenever the voltage changes
Note — click a cell and type the CC number it should send
Menu — Reset MIDI (Panic) clears the device of anything this module has sent
Turns sixteen gates from the patch into MIDI note on and off messages sent out to a device, for playing a drum machine from a sequencer
Rising past 2V sends a note on for the note printed in the cell above, and falling below 0.1V sends the note off; the velocity sent is 100
Note — click a cell and type the note it should send; the grid starts at C2 in the lower left corner and climbs by a semitone across each row
Menu — Velocity from gate amplitude takes the velocity from the voltage instead, 10V giving 127; Reset MIDI (Panic) clears the device of anything this module has sent
An empty panel for spacing modules apart in the rack; drag either edge to set its width, down to a minimum of 3HP
A panel of editable text for notes about the patch; click it and type, and what you write is saved with the patch
